quest.title: The Recollector's Path
quest.description: The training is approaching its conclusion. Zurvan's approval is but a step away...\n
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x10, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: You look much happier than when last we spoke. Seems things have gone well?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmm. From what I've learned doing these tasks, I have grown. For now...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: You are worthy of being called Bloomguard?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: No... not yet. There is still a final portion of the task that I need to complete.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Until all the tasks are done, until your respect is earned, I am not finished. Only then can the "Twin-Horned Chaplet" truly belong to me.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Oh? Looks like you're actually beyond your rebellious phase after all, just as was claimed.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: E—Elder, you... still remember that? Forget, I beg of you!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Haha. Regardless, it's good to see that your spirits have returned.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}. Paimon. Please be witnesses to the truth of whether Sorush is worthy of the Twin-Horned Chaplet.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Then I will await you at the end. See you soon.

talks.objective: Head to the specified location and complete the trial
Head to the specified location and complete the trial

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Tunigi Hollow... this was the epicenter of the disaster. Though all seems calm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's not hard to think of how things were then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: These crystals are huge... A lot bigger than even Wenut! And to think it's Sorush's responsibility to handle future problems here...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Is this not the most essential duty a Bloomguard should uphold? In addition, Sorush should also expect this of herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's what they say, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Do you not trust me? Hmph. I did not realize I was at the stage that even the Pale Floater thinks so little of me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, Sorush's arrogance makes its grand return!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not sure if that's a good thing or a bad thing.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph. Why do both of you still harbor such doubt in me after our time together? My pride has never been born of blind arrogance.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmm. You should be well aware that I fully understand my past mistakes.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Before, I placed reputation above action, but now, as I have learned, this is an act of purest neglect.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Just as Simurgh became the divine bird through her sacrifice, I will become the Bloomguard by my deeds and hear my name rightfully sung in praise of my service.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Additionally, I have completed all the assignments you have given me, Elder. Now, even you must admit that I am one worthy of the title of Bloomguard, worthy of the Twin-Horned Chaplet.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I indeed have no objection to the choice made by the Khvarena.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: What? Did you expect me to object?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: No... I merely... did not expect you to agree so easily, Elder...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I expected a few rough words at least?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm not nearly so vicious.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: About the responsibilities of a Bloomguard... I did not actually gain any knowledge from the Chaplet...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Is this because I still do not embody the traits of the Bloomguard fully? Do I still lack training?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: For this... The title of Bloomguard might be inherited, but the duties are always variable...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I see.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: To state it simply: there are no fixed rules, and even more, there are no specific judging standards. Usually, the Khvarena's choice is final.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Huh? So, you're saying...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: I will not be taking the Twin-Horned Chaplet from you.

choices.text: Now you don't need to worry about the top of your head getting cold.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Missing the point!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I understand! This must be part of the test!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Seems like Sorush is having an epiphany...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You are a forgetful one, Pale Floater. I just said it! To pass these tests, besides competence and observation, the most important thing is understanding my past mistakes.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Even if the outcome was already determined, would it not be retreading the path of folly if I cast aside all that I have learned during training? So, I think this must be the last test my elder has left me.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: To a worthy Bloomguard this is but a simple task. This is a sign of your complete trust in me, Elder.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: I didn't expect you to see right through me. The Khvarena chose well.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: #But your changes... I suppose {NICKNAME} and Paimon bear some credit for that.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Indeed! My esteemed Yasnapati and the Pale Floater are both beings of merit.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Though I wish to say that I am potent enough alone... I believe that with their aid, the extinguishing of the Sign of Apaosha will be no difficult task.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: How very reliable. Don't forget, Mihir and Rashnu will also be able to assist you.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Worry not, Elder! Leave everything to me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon keeps thinking that Zurvan might have planned this... But seeing Sorush this happy, Paimon can't really complain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, as Zurvan said herself, the Khvarena's choice is final. That means that Zurvan can't change it either, right?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Oh, ho ho... You really think so?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa... That's a little scary...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Tunigi Hollow from before... the epicenter of the disaster of years past...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Paimon didn't think Sorush would really be able to extinguish the Sign of Apaosha and solve all the trouble happening here...

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Extinguishing the Sign of Apaosha is but the duty of the Bloomguard. Sorush only did as she should.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was all thanks to Mihir and Rashnu's help.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. And we put in plenty of work too.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Splendid! It's so nice of you, my Yasnapati and the Pale Floater, to look beyond the person of greatest importance: me.
